The core operator is convolutional feature extraction, where input video frames are transformed into feature maps using learned kernels. This is modeled as a linear transformation followed by a ReLU activation: Y = ReLU(Conv(X; K) + b). The CNN’s ability to classify football actions stems from its hierarchical representation learning, where early layers detect edges and textures, while deeper layers capture semantic features like player poses and movement trajectories. Real-time mistake monitoring uses these features to compute a loss function across player positions, identifying deviations from expected behavior. Player ability evaluation leverages the trained CNN to project player performance into a latent space, enabling probabilistic comparisons against benchmarks. These primitives form a closed-loop system: CNN extracts features → Mistake detection identifies anomalies → Ability evaluation quantifies skill → Coaching decisions adapt strategy.
